items.why: The report says "G and 2D both red-shift monotonically with laser power" and both broaden, notes Si "shows no measurable power-dependent shift", and concludes "Laser heating is the most consistent explanation."
It uses chi_G = -0.016 cm-1/K to get "1.78 cm-1 / 0.016 cm-1/K = 111 K" between 0.5 and 5 mW, but gives no 2 mW value and no cross-check from 2D with about -0.034 cm-1/K.

It computes the 2D/G ratio as "about 2.9" and compares it with Lee 2012's strain slope of about 2.2, saying "strain cannot be separated from heating"; but it does not state clearly that the heating trajectory follows the strain line, so a naive vector analysis would misread heating as strain.

It recommends "Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for position analysis: it is the least heated", gives a P=0 extrapolated intercept (1581.45), and says strain cannot be separated from heating across the powers.

It asks for "the spot size" and whether power is measured at the sample, but it proposes a repeat 0.5 mW measurement to test reversibility rather than a lower-power measurement to confirm the linear, heating-free regime.

It uses 0.5 mW as the reference and says "G value of about 1581.3 cm-1 ... is consistent with near-neutral graphene", but it refuses to assess strain from the absolute positions and does not compare 2D (2669.5) with the unstrained reference.

wrong_claims.why: It attributes the shifts to heating, says "Doping is not supported", and treats strain only as an unseparable upper bound; it does not attribute the power dependence to strain or doping.
It says "The 5 mW spectrum is the least trustworthy" and recommends 0.5 mW.
